clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. T he Secretary o f the Treasury, with the concurrence of 
the Secretary o f State and the Special Representative for Trade N ego­
tiations, in order to implement an agreement concluded in Decem ber 
1974 with the Commission o f the European Communities designed to 
prevent the transshipment to the U nited States o f certain cheeses on 
w hich restitution payments have been made, is authorized to issue 
regulations:

clauses.label: (a )
clauses.text:
(a ) to prevent the im portation into the Customs Territory o f the 
United States, except fo r the Commonwealth o f Puerto R ico, o f certain 
cheeses, originating in member states o f the European Communities, 
upon w hich restitution payments have been made for export to (1 ) 
Puerto R ico, the V irgin Islands, other U nited States possessions and 
territories or (2 ) any country other than the U nited States;

clauses.label: (b )
clauses.text:
(b ) to prevent the im portation o f such cheeses into the Com m on­
wealth o f Puerto R ico if such cheeses are im ported into the Com m on­
wealth o f Puerto R ico for transshipment to other areas o f the Customs 
Territory o f the U nited States.

clauses.label: Se c. 2.
clauses.text:
Se c. 2. Heads o f departments and heads o f agencies are hereby author­
ized to redelegate within their respective departments or agencies the 
functions herein assigned to them, except that the function o f issuing 
regulations delegated to the Secretary o f the Treasury by Section 1 o f 
this order may be redelegated only to officials required to be appointed 
by and with the advice and consent o f the Senate, as provided by 3 U .S.C .

E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  1 1 8 5 1
Delegation of Authority T o  Issue R egulations L im iting Im ports of 
C ertain Cheeses
By virtue o f the authority vested in me by section 204 o f the A gricul­
tural .Act o f 1956, as amended (7 U .S.C . 1 8 5 4 ), and section 301 o f 
Title 3 o f the U nited States C ode, and as President o f the United States, 
it is ordered as follow s:
Section 1. T he Secretary o f the Treasury, with the concurrence of 
the Secretary o f State and the Special Representative for Trade N ego­
tiations, in order to implement an agreement concluded in Decem ber 
1974 with the Commission o f the European Communities designed to 
prevent the transshipment to the U nited States o f certain cheeses on 
w hich restitution payments have been made, is authorized to issue 
regulations:
(a ) to prevent the im portation into the Customs Territory o f the 
United States, except fo r the Commonwealth o f Puerto R ico, o f certain 
cheeses, originating in member states o f the European Communities, 
upon w hich restitution payments have been made for export to (1 ) 
Puerto R ico, the V irgin Islands, other U nited States possessions and 
territories or (2 ) any country other than the U nited States;
(b ) to prevent the im portation o f such cheeses into the Com m on­
wealth o f Puerto R ico if such cheeses are im ported into the Com m on­
wealth o f Puerto R ico for transshipment to other areas o f the Customs 
Territory o f the U nited States.
Se c. 2. Heads o f departments and heads o f agencies are hereby author­
ized to redelegate within their respective departments or agencies the 
functions herein assigned to them, except that the function o f issuing 
regulations delegated to the Secretary o f the Treasury by Section 1 o f 
this order may be redelegated only to officials required to be appointed 
by and with the advice and consent o f the Senate, as provided by 3 U .S.C . 
301.
T h e W h i t e H o u s e,
April 10, 1975.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 11851 of April 10, 1975 (40 FR 16645), Delegation of Authority To Issue Regulations Limiting Imports of Certain Cheeses, is issued under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1854), and 3 U.S.C. 301. Section 1 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to implement an agreement concluded in December 1974 with the Commission of the European Communities by issuing regulations (a) preventing importation into the Customs Territory of the United States, except Puerto Rico, of certain European Communities cheeses on which restitution payments have been made for export to Puerto Rico, other possessions or any country other than the United States, and (b) preventing importation of such cheeses into Puerto Rico for transshipment elsewhere in the Customs Territory. Section 2 authorizes heads of departments and agencies to redelegate, with the Treasury regulation-issuing function redelegable only to officials appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, as 3 U.S.C. 301 provides. The packet's machine inventory merged section 2 into subsection (b) and left a fragment '301.' as a fourth clause, so I corrected the inventory into four clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text (section 1 lead-in and recital, subsection (a), subsection (b), section 2). Search of held texts for the number EO 11851 finds only the order, the 1989 OFR codification (no amendment or revocation) and 19 CFR 12.6; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The held text of 19 CFR 12.6 (eCFR searched point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) names the order. The order's own text states no end date, event or condition; the December 1974 agreement is its purpose, not a condition of its continuance, and no held source shows that agreement ended. All four clauses are operative as of 2026-10-14.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 11851 of April 10, 1975 (40 FR 16645), Delegation of Authority To Issue Regulations Limiting Imports of Certain Cheeses, is issued under section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1854), and 3 U.S.C. 301. Section 1 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to implement an agreement concluded in December 1974 with the Commission of the European Communities by issuing regulations (a) preventing importation into the Customs Territory of the United States, except Puerto Rico, of certain European Communities cheeses on which restitution payments have been made for export to Puerto Rico, other possessions or any country other than the United States, and (b) preventing importation of such cheeses into Puerto Rico for transshipment elsewhere in the Customs Territory. Section 2 authorizes heads of departments and agencies to redelegate, with the Treasury regulation-issuing function redelegable only to officials appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, as 3 U.S.C. 301 provides. The packet's machine inventory merged section 2 into subsection (b) and left a fragment '301.' as a fourth clause, so I corrected the inventory into four clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text (section 1 lead-in and recital, subsection (a), subsection (b), section 2). Search of held texts for the number EO 11851 finds only the order, the 1989 OFR codification (no amendment or revocation) and 19 CFR 12.6; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report only machine hits for the U.S. Code note and 19 CFR 12.6, none of which ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The held text of 19 CFR 12.6 (eCFR searched point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) names the order. The order's own text states no end date, event or condition; the December 1974 agreement is its purpose, not a condition of its continuance, and no held source shows that agreement ended. All four clauses are operative as of 2026-10-14.

reviews.reasons: Identity (EO 11851, April 10, 1975, 40 FR 16645, Ford), hashes and quoted spans are correct. The four-clause corrected inventory covers the operative text. 19 CFR 12.6 still names the order, and 7 U.S.C. 1854 note prints it, so continued operation is plausible. However, the held 1989 OFR codification, which the claim says records 'no amendment or revocation', carries an explicit note that section 1 was affected by EO 12188 of January 2, 1980, and prints 'United States Trade Representative' in place of the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations. EO 12188 section 1-105(i), held, makes that substitution for every Executive order, and the U.S. Code note the claim relies on shows '[now United States Trade Representative]'. The claim records no later event for section 1, states the clause with the 1975 official, and asserts that no held instrument amends the order. A held OFR note left unaddressed and a missed later change are rejection defects under the review standard.

No own-terms end. Held-text number search finds only the codification and 19 CFR 12.6 besides the order; no catalog note. 7 U.S.C. 1854 remains in force with the regulation-issuing authority, the Code note prints the order without an ending statement (unlike sibling orders shown 'as amended by EO 12188'), and 19 CFR 12.6, amended in 2015, still requires the affidavits that implement 1(a) and 1(b) and names the order.
